statusText: Mapped policy state: EA_ON. Tail 7% (low) with Nasdaq-100 futures inside the CME weekend halt and no live price path available.
recommendation: Tail remains far below the block threshold because no tradable price path can form while index futures are halted through 22:00 UTC on Sunday. Stress is elevated on 2007-high Treasury yields, a reported lean toward further Fed tightening in October and December, and the refusal of Iran's seven-day Hormuz proposal, which leaves an unpriced geopolitical variable to be absorbed at the reopen.
headline: Weekend halt with Hormuz proposal refused: Tail low, Stress elevated on 2007-high yields
body: Nasdaq-100 index futures have been halted since Friday 21:00 UTC and do not reopen until 22:00 UTC on Sunday, ten hours beyond the end of this forecast window, so every hour assessed here sits inside a closed market. Friday's cash session ended constructively and without pathological structure: NDX closed 30,608.14, up 0.42%, inside a 30,413.59-30,667.56 range and below its 30,770.63 52-week high, while the S&P 500 added 0.51% to 7,743.41, the Dow 0.93% to 51,828.62 and the Nasdaq Composite 0.48% to 27,068.72. On the week the Nasdaq Composite gained about 2%, the S&P 500 1.2% and the Dow 0.3%. VIX fell 5.11% to 14.87, near the low of its 14.68-15.94 range. Delayed latest-session megacap data was dispersed rather than one-way, with MSFT up 3.66% and QCOM up 3.97% against META down 3.33% and INTC down 3.45%; six of eight names were higher but dispersion was 1.92 points, which reads as rotation rather than the persistent directional efficiency Tail measures. That feed carries no source as-of and cannot establish current NQ structure. The geopolitical position is now better documented and more contradictory than at the previous assessment. The Wall Street Journal reports that Washington has refused Iran's seven-day proposal to reopen the Strait of Hormuz and halt regional fighting, and that renewed strikes are expected only after the November congressional elections; Iran's plan required the release of roughly $12 billion in frozen funds, the lifting of oil sanctions and an end to the port blockade. Against that, a U.S. official describes the mediated discussions as positive and constructive and says Washington is in no hurry to respond. Conflicting signals of this kind reduce directional conviction and leave an unpriced variable for the reopen; because the reported strike timeline is post-midterm rather than imminent, they raise Stress and weekend gap risk rather than establishing a near-term pathological price path. The strait itself remains far below its pre-crisis transit baseline, which keeps a premium in energy: WTI settled at $92.41, down 2.33% on the day and about 7.4% on the week but still 12.4% higher on the month, with Brent at $104.32. The durable stress source remains rates. H.15 puts the 10-year at 5.18% and the 30-year at 5.47% for Sep 24, the 10-year at its highest since 2007 and the long bond since 2004, with the 2-year at 4.87%; the 30-year fixed mortgage rate reached 7.45%, a more than two-year high. Saturday reporting notes that markets are leaning toward further Fed tightening at the October and December meetings, with Cleveland's Hammack attributing higher yields to solid growth while others point to fiscal supply. Tail is therefore held in a 7-9 band across the window: a pathological price path cannot form in a closed market, and no observed shallow pullback, failed retracement or session-extreme holding exists to support a higher reading. The small late-window increment is accumulated gap risk ahead of the reopen, not observed structure. Stress is elevated at 48% and drifts to 52% as unpriced weekend information accumulates into a single reopening print, with a heavy macro week following: JOLTS and Consumer Confidence Tuesday, Core PCE and final Q2 GDP Wednesday alongside Micron's fiscal Q4 report after the close, ISM Manufacturing Thursday and September payrolls Friday. Confidence is high at 81% on verified levels, yields, oil, volatility and calendar coverage, decaying to 74% as Friday's settlement ages with no live price path to refresh it. Mapped policy state: EA_ON.
